text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliamentary support for the Islamist-led government -- facing an opposition censure motion -- is falling away. A third government minister has resigned from her post saying she was being barred by ultra-conservatives in both alliance parties from passing legislation.
- Turkey has begun to import more fruit at the expense of home-grown produce, which is left to rot.
- An opposition MP said he was offered "incentives" by the government if he promised to oppose a censure motion against the ruling alliance.
- The international monetary fund says that the most serious problem in Turkey is inflation, currently at around 80 percent.
- A government MP asked conservative deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller to end the ruling alliance as it no longer has any public support.
- Rebel government MP Yalim Erez has outlined the framework for a new Islamist-free government.
- Ciller is "threatening" government MPs wavering over whether to support the opposition censure motion with sackings or early elections.
- Thousands of secularists called for the resignation of the Islamist-led government in a rally.
- The Islamist-led government wants elections in November.
